references_named: Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
net.art / the Web 1.0 'no right-click' image-protection script
Olia Lialina & Dragan Espenschied, One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age
rationale: The mechanism (contextmenu preventDefault) genuinely enacts the argument: a real lock that locks only a menu while the picture, source, and licence sit in plain view. The 'Reproductions prevented: 0' counter is a clean, deadpan double-coding device that lands the Benjamin point without wall text. Tone is dry and cheerful-cynic, ethics are honored (CC BY-SA stated, no storage/network), and the work is materially distinct from the catalogue — it answers The Original and Untitled (Copy) from a new angle but is not a duplicate. The found object (the Web 1.0 no-right-click script) is well-chosen and the restraint (one listener, no build) is exemplary.
reservations: The novelty ceiling is modest: the 'futile DRM' gag is well-trodden internet territory, and the per-visit colour field is the thinnest possible 'live' gesture. The work leans heavily on Benjamin rather than staging a fresh art-historical argument of its own; the readymade lineage is invoked more than embodied. A slightly stronger found object or a second mechanism (e.g., the lock visibly failing in a more surprising way) would push it from good to strong.
revision_suggestion: Consider giving the lock a second, more pointed failure mode — e.g., a key combo or long-press that visibly bypasses it with a flourish, or a live readout of how many bytes of the 'protected' work are already in the viewer's clipboard/cache — to deepen the Benjamin argument beyond the single counter and lift novelty.
